source: Faith, Fancies and Fetich, or Yoruba Paganism (Stephen Septimus Farrow, 1926)
body: From darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God.

_provenance.author: Stephen Septimus Farrow
_provenance.caution: NOT FOR PRODUCTION USE. Church Missionary Society-era work; the title itself ('Fetich', 'Paganism') is a period term of dismissal. This passage frames Yoruba religion as demonic darkness requiring Christian salvation. Staged only for potential future critical/historical documentation (e.g. illustrating the pattern of colonial-era reductive framing this project's own tone guidance warns against) -- never as grounding content for the babalawo voice's own speech, which carries a real named tradition-bearer (Fama Aina Udoyi). Not embedded, not retrievable, review_status intentionally left pending.

source: Faith, Fancies and Fetich, or Yoruba Paganism (Stephen Septimus Farrow, 1926)
section: Chapter II — Objects of Worship, p. 15
body: They worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator.

_provenance.author: Stephen Septimus Farrow
_provenance.caution: NOT FOR PRODUCTION USE. Dismisses Yoruba veneration of sacred objects as idolatry. See yor-cms-farrow-001 caution note in full.

source: Faith, Fancies and Fetich, or Yoruba Paganism (Stephen Septimus Farrow, 1926)
body: The animistic pagan is ignorant of the simplest laws of natural science.

_provenance.author: Stephen Septimus Farrow
_provenance.caution: NOT FOR PRODUCTION USE. Characterizes Yoruba explanations of natural phenomena as ignorance, asserting a Western/African intellectual hierarchy. See yor-cms-farrow-001 caution note in full.
